children: HDFC Bank on Saturday reported a 4.7 percent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the second quarter of FY27, broadly meeting market expectations. The private sector lender's net interest income (NII) rose 9.7 percent to Rs 34,619.2 crore, while asset quality improved both sequentially and on a year-on-year basis.
A CNBC TV18 poll had projected a 5 percent increase in net profit to Rs 19,567 crore and a 10 percent rise in NII to Rs 34,861 crore. Both reported figures were within 1 percent of the estimates.
HDFC Bank's net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.16 percent on total assets and 3.32 percent on interest-earning assets during the July-September quarter.
Provisions and contingencies stood at Rs 3,570 crore for the quarter, while the total credit cost ratio was 0.44 percent.
Asset quality improves

HDFC Bank's gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.11 percent as of September 30, 2026, from 1.17 percent in the preceding quarter and 1.24 percent a year earlier. Excluding non-performing assets in the agricultural segment, the GNPA ratio stood at 0.87 percent, compared with 0.91 percent in June 2026 and 0.99 percent in September 2025.
The net NPA ratio stood at 0.37 percent at the end of the September quarter.
Advances and deposits register double-digit growth
The bank's gross advances rose 16.3 percent year-on-year to Rs 32,19,500 crore as of September 30, 2026, while advances under management grew 15.3 percent.
Retail loans increased 11.7 percent, small and mid-market enterprise loans grew 23.5 percent, and corporate and other wholesale loans expanded 16.4 percent.
Average advances under management stood at Rs 31,87,200 crore during the quarter, up 14.1 percent year-on-year and 4.9 percent sequentially.

Total deposits increased 18.8 percent year-on-year to Rs 33,27,400 crore at the end of September. Average deposits rose 16.8 percent to Rs 31,66,400 crore, registering sequential growth of 5.1 percent.
CASA deposits grew 10.8 percent year-on-year, accounting for 31.6 percent of total deposits. Time deposits increased 22.8 percent.
Capital adequacy and operating performance

HDFC Bank's capital adequacy ratio under Basel III stood at 18.9 percent as of September 30, 2026, compared with 20 percent a year earlier and a regulatory requirement of 11.9 percent. The Tier 1 capital adequacy ratio stood at 17.2 percent, while the Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio was 17.1 percent.

The bank reported net revenue of Rs 48,450 crore for the quarter, compared with Rs 45,900 crore a year earlier. Other income stood at Rs 13,830 crore, including fees and commissions of Rs 9,690 crore. Treasury trading gains declined to Rs 780 crore from Rs 2,390 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Operating expenses increased to Rs 18,970 crore from Rs 17,980 crore a year earlier, while the cost-to-income ratio stood at 39.1 percent. The bank said net profit excluding treasury trading gains grew approximately 12.6 percent year-on-year.
HDFC Bank stock performance

HDFC Bank shares closed 0.28 percent higher at Rs 728.85 on Friday, ahead of the results announcement. The stock has declined 26.5 percent so far in 2026, compared with an 11.5 percent fall in the Nifty 50. The bank's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 11.24 lakh crore.
